chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the children when they form rows in the obligatory prayer. He said: 'Do not delay them from the obligatory prayer, and separate them (from one another).'

key_terms.لَا تُؤَخِّرُوهُمْ: do not delay them / do not keep them back

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on children joining congregational prayers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the pedagogical approach to integrating children into congregational prayer, emphasizing early exposure to the ritual rather than exclusion. The instruction to separate them (farriqū baynahum) reflects the scholarly understanding that while their presence is encouraged for habituation, their distinct rows or spacing prevent the disruption of the adult congregation's focus (khushūʿ). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on gradual religious socialization within the communal framework.
